title: Relevance Feedback: Visual Guide
outline: 1. Which Side Moves | a toggle between tuning the document side (k1, b, mu) and the query side, with rounds of Rocchio applied to q0 = [1,0] and a live 'user wording as a share of q' readout | no document-side dial can give an absent term a query weight, so feedback changes the query itself — and repeated rounds erode the original-query anchor

2. Move The Query Vector | alpha, beta and gamma sliders over the lesson's own example (q0 = [1,0], relevant centroid [0.5,1.5], nonrelevant [0,1]) plotted in 2-D with the full arithmetic printed | alpha anchors, beta pulls toward the relevant centroid and gamma pushes off the nonrelevant one, so term 2 reaches weight 1.0 without ever being typed — and gamma stays small because nonrelevance is diverse

3. The Interpolation Dial | a lambda slider over RM3's mixture of the query model (database 0.5, timeout 0.5) with the feedback model (connection 0.35, pool 0.25, database 0.20, timeout 0.20), plus a switch for which side lambda names | at 0.6 on the original the intent stays dominant (0.38 / 0.38 / 0.14 / 0.10), and the same number read as the feedback weight produces a different query — which is how drift and irreproducible configs happen

4. Depth Drift Duplicates | two first-pass result lists (ambiguous 'jaguar' and the rare identifier 'ERR-5521 timeout') with a feedback-depth slider and tappable documents to drop, showing intent mix and independent documents after dedup | PRF turns ranking errors into expansion evidence, so mixed intents average into a useless centroid, boilerplate dilutes a rare identifier, and near-duplicates count as one piece of evidence

5. Anchor Then Expand | five expansion channels from Rocchio to generative rewriting compared on what they add, local vs global, explainability and cost, with an anchor-weight slider and a candidate-diversity control | the lineage is one move with different generators, and the inherited rules are keep an anchor to the original query, fuse both representations, and make candidates intent-diverse rather than numerous
